record.what_it_does: Cloud communications platform API for SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email, video and verification.
record.auth_notes: REST API uses HTTP Basic with Account SID + Auth Token, or API Key SID + Secret (preferred). OAuth2 client-credentials exists for some newer APIs, and Twilio Connect/OAuth for ISV apps (from memory, not verified here). No standard multi-user OAuth for generic API access; each user would supply their own SID and key/secret.
record.access_notes: Free trial account with trial credit, from memory (not verified on a fetched page). Trial accounts are limited to verified numbers and add a message prefix. Production use needs an upgraded pay-as-you-go account. Pricing is per-usage, so there is no free tier.
record.api_breadth_notes: Many product APIs: Messaging, Voice, Lookup, Verify, Conversations, Studio, Video, Sync, Proxy, TaskRouter, IAM and others. Likely hundreds of operations.
record.mcp_notes: @twilio-alpha/mcp, from github.com/twilio-labs/mcp. It is an alpha and experimental package. Twilio's support page says Twilio doesn't officially offer or support an MCP implementation. The twilio/ai repo has a hosted docs-search MCP at mcp.twilio.com/docs. Classified as official_local with low confidence because of the conflicting support status.
record.blocker_notes: The API is open and has an OpenAPI spec. Caveats: auth is per-account SID and key rather than a multi-user OAuth flow. Trial accounts are restricted. Real messaging needs a paid account plus regulatory work (A2P 10DLC registration, sender verification). Test credentials cover only a few endpoints.

evidence.quote: each product corresponds to an API.
Twilio doesn't charge your account, update the state of your account, or connect to real phone numbers.
Twilio does not officially offer or support an MCP implementation, an alpha version is available.

record.needs_human: The auth page and signup/trial pages weren't fetched, so the auth methods and trial terms come from memory. Check Twilio's current OAuth support and trial limits. Confirm whether the alpha MCP counts as vendor-official. The MCP evidence quote comes from a search snippet, not a page I opened.
